markdown: ## 8. Media

Night, fog and rain reduce drone effectiveness; this is when rotations and infiltration happen. Scale the depth up by era, from about 3 km (2023) to 25+ km (2026). Sources: rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments, pravda-2026-levytska-magyar-kill-zone.
- **Detection → strike latency as a core stat.**
  - About 3–5 minutes with an organic drone; 20–30 minutes through an HQ; hours to days at operational level (2022–23).
  - Ukrainian digital tools (GIS Arta at 30–45 s, Avengers detection at 2.2 s) shorten the loop.
  - Loss of a C2 bearer (Starlink-cutoff event, EW) lengthens it and can cause friendly fire.
  - 2025–26 figures are thin and not independent. Russia's Glaz/Groza cut its drone-to-artillery loop "from hours to minutes" (CSIS, from Russian developer channels). Euromaidan Press says Delta cut Ukraine's detection-to-strike time "from roughly 20 minutes to a few" (unattributed). RUSI gives slower timings for everything else: 24–48 hours for each of the first three attack phases, and 2–3 hours from UGV rendezvous to medical post [src:csis-2026-bondar-russian-c2] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-hryfon-zakhid] [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms].

None was independently verified.
- **Internal criticism.** In 2022 nationalist milbloggers criticised Putin and Medvedev's silence after Medvedev's "red line" threats [src:isw-2022-10-09-roca]. In 2023 they faulted the neglect of maritime security in favour of checking cars [src:isw-2023-07-17-roca].
- **Retaliation framing.** Russia presented the 10 Oct 2022 missile strike and the 18 Jul 2023 Odesa strike as retaliation [src:isw-2022-10-10-roca; pravda-2023-peskov-odesa-revenge].
## 11. Open questions/gaps

Through 2023, missiles and sea drones together drove most of the fleet from Sevastopol to Novorossiysk (October 2023) [src:pravda-2023-mt-anderson-bsf-novorossiysk]. Ukraine opened its own export corridor along the western coast on 16 Aug 2023 [src:pravda-2023-first-ship-corridor].

- **Ammunition and launchers in the south.** No source gives the number of GMLRS rockets fired at the Kherson crossings or how many launchers were allotted to OC South.
- **Date of the first bridge strike.** ISW reports 19 July [src:isw-2022-07-19-roca], while Miller gives 20 July in one article and implies 19 July in the other [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far].
- **Was the road bridge ever reopened?** Wikipedia says repairs were completed by 23 August. Satellite imagery two days later showed 16 holes and ferries in use [src:wikipedia-antonivka-road-bridge] [src:isw-2022-08-29-roca].
- **VDV composition.** Miller says the whole VDV except the 106th Division was on the right bank, while ISW names the 106th among the withdrawing units [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:isw-2022-11-09-roca]. The ORBAT figures come from open sources and Ukrainian claims, and are partly unverified.
- **Size of the Russian force and of the withdrawal.** Estimates range from 20,000 to 42,370 (see section 1).
- **Equipment losses.** There is no Kherson-specific Oryx-type count of equipment destroyed or abandoned in July–November, or of the trophies taken in November.
- **Ukrainian losses.** Ukraine has never published figures. Only unit-level anecdotes and Russian claims exist.
- **Date of the strike on the 247th Regiment and Chornobaivka.** The sources give 22 or 23 August [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].
- **Did weather force the withdrawal?** Miller argues that winter ice would have stopped ferries, but ERA5 shows no daily minimum below 0 °C through 15 November [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal] [src:openmeteo-era5-kherson-2022]. Treat the freeze as a looming threat, not a fact of the window.
- **Paywalled sources not checked first-hand.** The Washington Post (29 Dec 2022) and NYT (Entous, 29 Mar 2025) accounts of the planning, Kovalchuk's dam test and his dismissal are cited only through Wikipedia's summary of them.
- **Coordinates.** The Darivka bridge itself was not geolocated; only the village centre is given. An Overpass query failed.

- **Ukrainian offence.** Kherson began on 29 August 2022 and drew in Russian reserves. Kharkiv followed on a thinly held front: Ukraine did not surprise Russia about its intentions, but did surprise it on timing [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. Ukraine advanced 75 km in four days (Balakliia, Izium, Kupiansk) against a Russian defence of "one tier" [src:euromaidan-2022-shandra-kharkiv]. At Kherson, Russia withdrew in good order across the Dnipro in October–November [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Russian response.** Russia declared mobilization, took the Dnipro as a barrier, and began building deliberate defence lines (the "Surovikin line") in Zaporizhzhia. By May 2023 its group of forces was about 420,000 strong [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

### Russia and the DNR
## 9. Terms
## 5. Systems and tactics in use

- **Russian assault style.** Meatgrinder describes a four-tier infantry system:
  - Disposable infantry came from DNR/LNR conscripts, Wagner convicts and under-trained mobilized men. They were first organised in companies of about 60, later in platoons of about 15, and attacked in fire teams of 2–5, with up to 5 teams on one axis.
  - The teams skirmished "often until killed". Some were shot by their own side when retreating, and Ukrainian troops report many appeared to be on amphetamines.
  - Specialised and assault troops were then sent against the Ukrainian positions this exposed [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
  - At Artemivske in December 2022, four UAVs flew over each assault group, covering reconnaissance, reserve routes, ambush detection and the commander's view.
- **Losses.** 19,547 Wagner fighters were killed at Bakhmut and a similar number seriously wounded. 88% of them were convicts; trained Wagner deaths averaged 40–60 a week. About 10,000 Ukrainians were killed or severely wounded in and around the city, and Russia held a 5:1 artillery advantage [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Russian penal units.** Storm-Z convict companies in regular units offered a pardon after six months and ended in August 2023. From late 2023 they were replaced by Storm-V, with no pardon and contracts lasting until the end of the war [src:ukrpravda-2024-isw-storm-v].
- **Vuhledar.** The ill-prepared January–February 2023 offensive "beginning in Vuhledar" was extremely costly. The Russian command appears to have judged it could "trade lives for time" [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Ukrainian defence.** Ukraine lost about 10,000 UAVs a month to Russian EW [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Ukrainian losses turned unfavourable once Russian artillery controlled the roads into Bakhmut [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**Command change.** Defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov was sacked in mid-July, which set off street protests. Special-operations commander Yevhen Khmara became acting minister on 16 Jul [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-khmara]. On 21 Jul Maj Gen **Mykhailo Drapatyi** replaced Syrskyi as Commander-in-Chief. Zelensky said the mid- and long-range strike programmes would continue unchanged [src:guardian-2026-murray-drapatyi].

- The Orlan-10 was the Russian workhorse. Russian units with their own UAVs could fire within 3–5 minutes of detection, against 20–30 minutes when the request went through a fire-control headquarters. ## 2. Timeline
**Weather and light on key nights.** Weather is modelled ERA5 reanalysis [src:openmeteo-era5-archive]; the moon is from USNO, computed for central Crimea [src:usno-rstt-oneday].
## 2. Timeline
**Defining features.** Russia's firepower-driven attrition against a Ukraine short of ammunition. Glide bombs "gave the VKS teeth" without air superiority [src:rusi-2025-watling-third-year].

- **DeepStateMap is the reference.** It is Ukrainian, run by the DeepState UA NGO, fed largely by Ukrainian military sources, and deliberately published 2–3 days late for operational security [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping]. Its visual grammar is simple. Semi-transparent area fills show control status (occupied, liberated, recently liberated, unknown/grey, pre-2022 occupied). Point icons mark Russian units, airfields and HQs, and arrows show "directions of attack" [src:deepstate-api-history]. Ukrainian positions are never shown [src:kyivpost-2025-ashcroft-inside-deepstate].
- **ISW/CTP is the Western reference.** Its legend is epistemic rather than just territorial. It separates *assessed* (evidence-backed) from *claimed* (asserted, unverified) and, since December 2025, draws a dedicated *infiltration areas* layer [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain]. Most Western outlets (e.g., the BBC) redraw ISW/CTP data [src:bbc-2022-ukraine-in-maps].
- **The front line has stopped being a line.** From 2025 on, drone "kill zones" and infiltration by small Russian groups turned the grey zone from a thin no-man's-land into a deep contact zone with overlapping positions. That forced DeepState (2026) and ISW (Dec 2025) to redefine their uncertainty categories [src:onlineua-2026-deepstate-legend] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping] [src:warontherocks-2026-maurin-front-line]. This is directly relevant to eras e8-drone-kill-zone and e9-counteroffensive-26.
- **Mapping is political.** DeepState has clashed publicly with Ukrainian commanders over encirclements and breakthroughs (Makarivka, Dec 2024; Dobropillia, Aug 2025). Flag-planting photo-ops by both sides are an information-war tactic that careful mappers refuse to map [src:devua-2024-deepstate-makarivka] [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-front-line-mapping].
- **Tactical UIs are a different world.** Delta (MoD situational awareness), Kropyva (Army SOS artillery/mapping tablet app), and the "Vezha" drone-stream module with Avengers AI are the Ukrainian military's own digital layers [src:wikipedia-delta] [src:militarnyi-2022-delta-unveiled] [src:forbes-2022-hambling-kropyva]. The Army of Drones Bonus "e-points" system turned video-verified strikes into a points economy with unit leaderboards and a marketplace [src:kyivpost-2026-korshak-epoints] [src:defensenews-2026-ruitenberg-epoints] [src:united24-2026-petriv-army-of-drones].
- **One consistent territory metric exists.** DeepState's undocumented history endpoint serves the full GeoJSON of every map version since 3 April 2022. Differencing month-end versions reproduces DeepState's own published monthly figures to within a few km² in most months, and gives Russian gains and Ukrainian recaptures separately (§2.7) [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:euromaidan-2026-tril-2025-4336].
- **Data rights are the main blocker.** DeepState has no documented API or open licence, although undocumented JSON endpoints exist and community scrapers use them. ISW's ArcGIS layers are public but carry "exclusive intellectual property… written consent" terms. ACLED requires a corporate licence for commercial use [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain] [src:acled-eula]. GeoConfirmed's free API is scoped to "research, journalism, and analytical use", and Liveuamap allows reuse "with reference" but sells its API [src:geoconfirmed-openapi] [src:liveuamap-about-terms]. Only the symbology renderer milsymbol is permissively (MIT) licensed [src:github-milsymbol].
### e8-drone-kill-zone (Mar 2025–Jan 2026)
## 8. Media

- **HIMARS/GMLRS against bridges.** GMLRS reaches about 80 km [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons], with a CEP "less than a meter" [src:militarnyi-2023-kozatskyi-himars-year]. Ukraine fired small salvoes at the same aim point: 8 rockets on 20 Jul, 7 at Darivka and the dam about 22 Jul, and 8 + 2 on 26–27 Jul. This cratered the deck rather than dropping spans, and the strikes were repeated whenever repairs began [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far] [src:isw-2022-07-27-roca] [src:isw-2022-08-25-roca]. TWZ reports that Ukraine deliberately hit only one small segment of the road bridge so that it could be repaired after liberation [src:twz-2022-newdick-antonivskyi-bridge]. Russian claims of interceptions (10 on 27 Jul, 44 on 30 Jul) are not borne out by footage [src:isw-2022-07-27-roca] [src:isw-2022-08-30-roca].
- **HIMARS against depots, HQs and trains.** Strikes hit the Kherson base on 10 Jul, the Nova Kakhovka depots, Radensk, the Brylivka train on 30 Jul, Chornobaivka, VDV regimental command posts on 1 Sep, and repair bases [src:isw-2022-07-12-roca] [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive] [src:isw-2022-07-31-roca] [src:isw-2022-09-01-roca] [src:isw-2022-10-22-roca]. 8–12 launchers wrecked most Russian depots in the south and Donbas within weeks, and depots moved beyond about 85 km [src:kyivindependent-2022-ponomarenko-himars]. The US counted 400+ HIMARS targets by 8 Sep [src:defenseone-2022-tucker-milley-himars]. After the strikes Russia could no longer stockpile ammunition beside its guns [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **Supporting precision.** Ukraine reportedly also used Excalibur and possibly Vulcano 155 mm rounds against crossings and depots [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far] [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal], and HARM against air defence (Russia claimed HARMs shot down over the bridge on 1 Sep) [src:forbes-2022-axe-attacking-everywhere] [src:isw-2022-09-01-roca].
- **Russian counters to interdiction.**
  - Radar reflectors on the bridges [src:isw-2022-07-31-roca].
  - Rapid deck repair, which was struck again each time [src:isw-2022-08-25-roca].
  - Pontoon ferries manoeuvred by river boats at up to six sites [src:wavellroom-2022-miller-river-too-far].
  - Repaired barges, then a barge bridge, then civilian ferries and barges commandeered from Kherson port, which were hard to target [src:isw-2022-08-21-roca] [src:isw-2022-10-22-roca] [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal].
  - A fuel pipeline along the rail bridge [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal].
  - Moving logistics deeper, to repair yards at Kalanchak and a new base about 70 km southeast of Kherson [src:isw-2022-10-13-roca] [src:isw-2022-11-12-roca].
Drones went from being scarce and quickly lost to being the main killer on the battlefield.

### e7-kursk-pokrovsk (Aug 2024–Mar 2025)
## 9. Sources

- **Three phases with different player verbs.**
  - *Act 1 (one day):* a survival and morale scene with no tactical win. The scoring gate is "garrison refuses, survives the bombardment, is captured alive". Decision 2 (the *Sapfir*) is a classic trap event to script.
  - *Act 2 (one afternoon and night):* a detection, timing and launch puzzle.
  - *Coda (about 10 weeks, compressed):* an interdiction board where the player cuts supply rather than storms the island.
- **Act 2 mechanics.** All are sourced:
  - Neptune's radar horizon is about 18 km, but a weather modifier lets it reach about 120 km under low cloud [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
  - The salvo is two missiles with about 6 min flight [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
  - The cruiser's AD readiness is a hidden state [src:navalnews-2022-ozberk-moskva-negligence]. Cloud also blinds TB2s and optical satellites [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-moskva-neptune].
  - The target can be confirmed by US/NATO input or not, and the debrief shows the dispute [src:nbc-2022-dilanian-us-intel-moskva].
  - The TB2 "decoy" should be an optional, contested modifier, not a requirement [src:forbes-2022-hambling-bayraktar-moskva].
- **Sinking model.** Two hits on a ship expected to need six or more [src:kyivpost-2023-tuzov-neptune-moskva]. The damage chain is fire, then AK-630 or Vulkan ammunition, then a tow in sea state 3, then a roll [src:intentpress-2025-neizhpapa-moskva-details] [src:guardian-2022-roth-moskva-photos]. Overnight pacing: about 11–13 h from launch (14:10 or about 16:00) to sinking (about 03:00) [src:pravda-2023-pohorilov-neptune-launch-video] [src:wikipedia-sinking-of-the-moskva].
- **Coda win band.** Russia abandons the island, with "no Ukrainian landing needed" and "assault fails" both historical.
  - Historical Russian attrition: about 4 Raptors, 1 Serna, multiple Tor/Pantsir/Strela-10, 1 Mi-8, 1 tug [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-tb2-ghost-snake-island] [src:navalnews-2022-ozberk-vasily-bekh] [src:ukrinform-2022-invaders-escape-snake-island].
  - Ukrainian costs: 1 Mi-14, about 10 assault troops and a boat, 1 Su-24MR [src:ppu-2024-bedzai] [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle] [src:wikipedia-snake-island-campaign].
  - Penalise holding the island with troops, which is not historical [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle].
- **Logistics as the target.** The island's supply should be a meter fed only by small craft and tugs. Each kill raises Russia's "cost to hold" until withdrawal triggers [src:zavhorodnii-2025-battles-snake-island] [src:dod-2022-vergun-snake-island-retreat]. After the *Moskva* is gone, Russian AD "umbrella" coverage drops to point defence only [src:navalnews-2022-sutton-curse-snake-island].
- **Artillery from the delta.** Guns at maximum range (40 km) move by pontoon at night (3–4 h each way). Metal decoys add radar noise, and the guns break down [src:militarnyi-2023-bohdana-snake-island].
- **Pacing.** Act 1 runs about 16 h of real events (03:00 to about 19:00); Act 2 about 11–13 h; the coda covers 15 Apr – 30 Jun with spikes on 2–8 May, 17 Jun and 20–30 Jun.

On 20 November 2025 Gerasimov told Putin that Kupiansk had been taken [src:isw-2025-11-21-roca]. By then Ukraine's counter-operation had already been running for weeks. Khartiia's search-and-destroy group and the Kupiansk Tactical Group cleared the forests and villages to the north, then pushed to the Oskil, cut the pipeline route and hunted the infiltrators building by building [src:ukrpravda-2026-kyrylenko-kupiansk-is-yours] [src:isw-2025-12-13-roca]. On 12 December Zelensky filmed himself at the town's entrance sign, and Khartiia announced that about 200 Russians were encircled inside [src:isw-2025-12-12-roca]. On 13 December the 429th "Achilles" regiment released video of the pipeline being blown with about three tonnes of explosives [src:defenseexpress-2025-achilles-pipeline-destroyed].
### e1-invasion (Feb–Apr 2022)

- **Kill-zone depth by era.** Model drone threat as a band with a density gradient that deepens over time:
  - 2022: sparse and short-range.
  - 2024: dense to about 3 km, thinning to 15 km, taskable to 40 km [src:rusi-2025-watling-reynolds-third-year].
  - 2025: 10–15 km lethal, with fiber-optic FPVs and Molniya reaching 40–50 km [src:ukrinform-2025-fedorov-fiber-optic-40km][src:mezha-2026-molniya].
  - 2026: 20–25 km on active axes, with 30 km expected by year-end [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-kill-zone-corps].
**Weather and light** (Open-Meteo reanalysis, Kyiv local time; Ukraine moved to summer time on 27 Mar) [src:openmeteo-2026-archive-mariupol-2022]:

- **Russian shell economy.** In Q1 2023 Russia fired 12,000–38,000 rounds a day, and days above 24,000 became rare. Use shifted from 152 mm guns to 120 mm mortars. Annual consumption was trending to about 7M against Ukrainian estimates of about 2.5M a year in Russian production [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **Russian reconnaissance-fire circuit (the Russian term for the kill chain).** Each axis commander keeps Orlan-10 orbits overhead, and the artillery brigade flies its own complex. Engagement takes about 3–5 min from UAV detection and 20–30 min from EW detection. The Strelets system links sensors to digital fire control. Krasnopol laser-guided shells and Lancet loitering munitions do counter-battery work and hunt guns [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **Russian air defence** now intercepts a share of GMLRS [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Excalibur's confirmed hit rate fell from more than 55% early in 2023 to 7% in July and 6% in August 2023. JDAM-ER, delivered from February 2023, lost accuracy within weeks, and a patch followed in May 2023 [src:stripes-2024-khurshudyan-jamming].
- **The VKS stays stand-off.** It uses FAB-500s with early glide kits from Su-35S out to about 70 km, in small but steady numbers, plus lofted S-8. Industry supplies about 40 long-range missiles a month. Tu-95 packages use Shaheds as pathfinders to find gaps in Ukrainian air defence [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].

Research pack for **bavovniatko**, covering the procedurally generated front-line landscape of eastern and southern Ukraine. Accessed 2026-09-28. Citations use the form `[src:<id>]` and resolve to `sources/06-terrain-geodata.yaml`. Era ids follow the canonical list (e1–e9).

**Weather and light** (ERA5 reanalysis, not observations [src:open-meteo-2026-era5-stepove-jan-2024]).
- *11 Jan 2024:* overcast, −3.6 to −2.1 °C, light snow (1.4 cm), snow cover about 12 cm.
- *12 Jan:* falls to −15.6 °C.
- *Light:* sunrise about 07:17 and sunset about 15:56 local time (UTC+2).
- *November 2023 (context):* morning fog opened windows for reinforcement and infiltration [src:euromaidan-2023-avdiivka-rain-fog].

**The bounded map.** The map is a strip of the lower Dnipro, about 35 km long, from the Antonivskyi bridges near Kherson upstream to Korsunka. The planned assault frontage, from the rail bridge to Krynky, was about 30 km [src:pravda-2024-kyrylenko-krynky-untold].

On the first day of the invasion, the cruiser *Moskva* and the patrol ship *Vasily Bykov* spent all of 24 Feb demanding over Channel 16 that Zmiinyi Island's garrison surrender. The garrison numbered about 80: border guards, marines of the 35th Brigade and a few others. Around 18:00 a border guard told the "Russian warship" to go f— itself. After a day of naval gunfire and Su-27/Su-34 air strikes, contact was lost about an hour later, and the whole garrison and the island's civilians were captured. First reports had them all dead [src:pravda-2022-romaniuk-zmiinyi-battle] [src:pravda-2023-deineko-16-border-guards]. The audio, published that night, became the war's rallying cry and a postage stamp. The prisoners came home over more than three years of exchanges, the last on 23 Jul 2025 [src:pravda-2022-romanenko-zmiinyi-audio] [src:ukrposhta-2022-warship-stamp] [src:pravda-2025-tyshchenko-last-zmiinyi-defender].

### e3-counteroffensives-22 (Sep–Nov 2022)

**What Russia had.** A **12:1 force ratio north of Kyiv**. It began with 2,433 barrel artillery systems against Ukraine's 1,176, and 3,547 MLRS against 1,680. Its main manoeuvre unit was the battalion tactical group (BTG) [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].

markdown: ## 9. Sources

- **Starlink cutoff, in phases.** The dates in the sources differ because they describe different steps:
  - *Trigger (late December 2025 – January 2026):* Rubikon and other units had fitted Starlink to BM-35 and Molniya-2 drones for strikes deep in the Ukrainian rear, against trains and vehicles on the E-50 Pokrovsk–Pavlohrad highway [src:isw-2026-02-01-roca] [src:isw-2026-02-05-roca]. On 29 January Fedorov said the MoD had contacted SpaceX within hours of Starlink-guided Russian drones appearing over Ukrainian cities [src:mod-2026-spacex-starlink-russian-uavs].
  - *First step (late January – 1 February):* a speed-based cutoff for terminals moving faster than about 75–90 km/h, which hit Starlink-equipped Shaheds and Molniyas [src:twz-2026-altman-rogoway-starlink-scramble] [src:isw-2026-02-01-roca]. On 1 February Musk wrote on X that the steps had worked, and Fedorov announced that only authorised terminals would be allowed [src:mod-2026-starlink-authorization-system].
  - *Registration (2 February):* a Cabinet resolution set up the whitelist. Civilians register at administrative service centres, businesses via Diia and the military via Delta [src:kyivindependent-2026-myronyshena-starlink-whitelist].
  - *Enforcement (5 February):* unregistered terminals went dark at about 03:00 Kyiv time. The same day Fedorov said Russian terminals were blocked and the whitelist was being updated once a day [src:kyivindependent-2026-starlink-catastrophe] [src:mod-2026-starlink-whitelist-operational].
  - ISW and outlets relaying it date the block to "1 February", meaning the first step. OSW and the Kyiv Independent date it to 5 February, meaning enforcement. United24's "early December" is an error [src:isw-2026-02-10-roca] [src:osw-2026-wilk-starlink-cutoff] [src:united24-2026-litnarovych-starlink-gains].
- **First effects:**
  - The General Staff reported fewer Russian assaults, and none at all in some sectors. Brigades reported fewer FPV sorties and fewer Molniya strikes on the rear [src:isw-2026-02-05-roca] [src:isw-2026-02-06-roca].
  - Russian units fell back on radios, cables, Wi-Fi bridges and cellular links, then brought in Yamal/Express satellite terminals and mesh networks [src:osw-2026-wilk-starlink-cutoff] [src:ukrinform-2026-starlink-c2].
  - Roskomnadzor throttled Telegram on 9–10 February, although units used it for horizontal coordination and air-defence cueing. Peskov said he could not imagine troops using messengers at the front, and milbloggers called that a lie [src:isw-2026-02-10-roca] [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-spencer-russian-comms-crisis].
  - Rubikon stopped posting location details [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-isw-rubikon-starlink]. Russian logistics units reportedly dropped Starlink-linked UGVs for crewed trucks and motorcycles [src:futuradoctrina-2026-ryan-starlink-surprise].
  - On 26 February Brig. Gen. Biletskyi (3rd Army Corps) said the cutoff had cut Russian drone effectiveness by roughly 20–40% in two weeks. He expected a partial recovery through other satellite links within one to two months, but not a return to Starlink-level efficiency for three to five years [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
- **Russian recovery, March–September:** partial. See §5 for the details [src:isw-2026-03-18-roca].
- **Territorial effect:**
  - More than 200 km² in the first five days (Atlantic Council), or 201 km² in one week per ISW data [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-spencer-russian-comms-crisis] [src:united24-2026-litnarovych-starlink-gains].
  - Zelensky claimed 745 km² by 12 August 2026 [src:wikipedia-2026-ukrainian-counteroffensive].
  - Ukraine's own terminals had been pre-registered and were largely unaffected [src:osw-2026-wilk-starlink-cutoff].
- **Operation Vivaldi (north of Lyman, end of May–September 2026)** is the best-documented Ukrainian ISR/C2 operation of the year:
  - *Secrecy:* the 3rd Army Corps attacked the Russian salient north of Lyman from about the end of May under an information blackout. Its commander, Biletskyi, confirmed the operation only on 15 September [src:hromadske-2026-lisova-vivaldi-phase1] [src:wikipedia-2026-ukrainian-counteroffensive]. SSO, border-guard and HUR units fought under the same tactical command [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
  - *Area:* the corps claims 75 km² cleared of infiltrators and 10 km² de-occupied in "season" one, then 40 km² more in season two (20 September: Shandryholove, Derylove, Drobysheve), for 125+ km² in all. Outside mappers put it higher: Molin at over 200 km², others at up to about 240 km². ISW judged the gains larger than disclosed but gave no figure. The "240 km²" is a mappers' estimate, not an ISW confirmation [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-isw-vivaldi-fortress-belt] [src:hromadske-2026-lisova-vivaldi-phase1].
  - *Reconnaissance aimed at C2:* brigade and corps reconnaissance mapped the Russian command nodes whose loss would break control of the sector. Heavy bomber drones then dropped kamikaze UGVs onto them, more than 10 km behind the line. Russia had to pull troops back to guard its command posts, and those troops were then missing from the defence [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting] [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-vivaldi-ugv-drop].
  - *Counter-ISR:* an air-defence and EW "dome" over the assault area blinded Russian drones so they "could not read the operation's design". Artillery and strike drones hit command posts, communications nodes, crossings and reserves. Assault groups moved through ravines and gullies [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-vivaldi-ugv-drop] [src:kyivindependent-2026-york-vivaldi-gains].
  - *Counter-drone:* in the preparatory phase the corps identified Rubikon as the unit most able to isolate the area and struck it. A Russian commander pulled Rubikon to the rear to recover just as the assault began. The corps says Russian drone units on the axis are at 70–90% strength [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting].
  - *Logistics:* the same intelligence effort found a diesel pipeline from Voronezh Oblast into occupied Luhansk Oblast. The corps says it covered about 50% of the daily fuel needs of Russian forces on the axis. Strikes on both ends forced Russia to dismantle it, and fuel now goes by truck on a 400 km run. Russia also moved the 20th Army / 144th Division repair base into Voronezh Oblast, lengthening the repair route to 250 km. Drone units could not refuel the generators that charge their batteries, and EW ran in reduced mode. ISW corroborated the supply problems [src:euromaidanpress-2026-zoria-vivaldi-targeting] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-isw-vivaldi-fortress-belt].
  - *Claims:* 3,000+ Russian casualties and 12,000+ drones in season one (corps figures, unverified). ISW assessed that Vivaldi made Russia's plan to encircle the Donetsk fortress belt from the north unfeasible [src:euromaidanpress-2026-isw-vivaldi-fortress-belt].
  - *Starlink:* no source ties Vivaldi to the Starlink cutoff directly. Biletskyi's corps is the one that reported a 20–40% drop in Russian drone effectiveness in February [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
- **Kill zone at 20–25+ km:**
  - Brovdi ("Magyar") puts it at 25+ km on both sides. He bases this on how regularly and densely strikes land, as tracked in the situational awareness system, not on the maximum range of individual drones [src:pravda-2026-levytska-magyar-kill-zone].
  - Brig. Gen. Lasiichuk (7th Air Assault Corps, Pokrovsk axis) gives 20–25 km now and expects 30 km by the end of 2026. Drones cause 70–80% of damage [src:euromaidanpress-2026-vivdych-kill-zone-corps].
  - The 107th TDF Brigade commander describes the distance troops must walk growing from 2 km to 3, 5, 10 and now 15+ km. Up to 20 km is "logistically difficult", and some trips to positions take three days [src:rbcukraine-2026-perch-kill-zone-foot].
  - On the Kramatorsk–Kostiantynivka road, vehicles run at up to 120 km/h under nets. Routine supply and rotations go on foot, and at least ten wrecked UGVs line the route [src:kyivindependent-2026-korovayny-road-kill-zone].
  - No strike-density map is public. The MoD's Mission Control does sort every mission by type and by depth band (20+ km, 50+ km) and records own losses by depth, so the data exists inside Delta [src:mod-2026-mission-control-cost-exchange]. The only open proxies are unit tallies (K-2: 258 strikes in April, 344 in May) and OSINT counts of strike videos [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island].
- **Ukrainian C2 at scale:**
  - Mission Control launched on 27 January 2026 as the national drone-management module inside Delta, replacing paper reports (forms 5.31/5.32) [src:mod-2026-mission-control-launch] [src:mod-2026-delta-6600-targets].
  - In June 2026 Delta logged 200,000+ drone strikes (6,600+ per day) and 75,000+ video streams per day. Confirmed strikes rose from 105,800 in January to 200,200 in June [src:mod-2026-delta-6600-targets].
  - The Avengers Labs dataset holds 5 million labelled images, and the auto-detector analyses 100,000+ drone streams per month [src:pravda-2026-levytska-avengers-labs].
- **UGVs** [src:united24-2026-kabachynskyi-ugv-25000] [src:united24-2026-kosoy-ugv-kill-zone] [src:mod-2026-ugv-9000-march] [src:mod-2026-ugv-triple]:
  - Monthly missions, from Delta data: 2,900+ (November 2025), then for January to August 2026 7,511 → 7,960 → 9,072 → 11,028 → 14,059 → 16,664 → 19,940 → **25,143**. The January–August total is about 112,000, 3.3 times the January rate by August. Most missions are logistics.
  - Units using UGVs: the two United24 counts do not conflict; they are two different MoD measures. Units active in a given month went from 67 (November 2025) to 167 (March 2026). Units that used UGVs at all went from 117 (2025) to 230 (2026 so far).
  - Plan: 25,000 UGVs contracted in the first half of 2026. One robot carries about 500 kg, the load of about 10 soldiers. The General Staff credits UGVs with up to 30% fewer personnel casualties (a claim) [src:euromaidanpress-2026-ugv-playbook].
  - Doctrine lags: about 200 models are in use, "basically every one" is modified by the unit, and best practice goes out of date in about six months [src:euromaidanpress-2026-ugv-playbook].
  - **Attrition:** a Khartia UGV commander says a robot used to last 12–15 missions, then 8–9, and now 3–4 near Kupiansk. The causes are mines, FPV and fibre-optic drones, and Russian crews assigned specifically to hunt UGVs. At 10–15 km/h most robots are too slow to cross logistics routes safely [src:euromaidanpress-2026-ugv-persian-elephants]. On the Kostiantynivka supply routes, where UGVs are the main resupply method, analysts counted at least 50 destroyed logistics UGVs by May [src:euromaidanpress-2026-axe-ugv-kostiantynivka]. RUSI observed a two to three hour wait at night between a UGV reaching the rendezvous and the casualty reaching the medical post [src:rusi-2025-watling-combined-arms]. No army-wide loss rate is published.
- **Road netting:** 1,066 km built between January and July 2026, reaching 9.2 km/day in June, with a target of 4,000 km by the end of 2026. Euromaidan Press says Russian reconnaissance and FPV drones work 15–30 km deep [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-net-tunnels-1000km] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-tril-net-tunnel-pace].
- **"Middle strike" / "Logistics Lockdown"** [src:kyivindependent-2026-rushton-middle-strike] [src:jamestown-2026-lapaiev-mid-range-drones] [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-kirichenko-drones-logistics]:
  - Ukrainian drones hit targets 20–200 km deep: fuel trucks, convoys, bridges and the R-280 "Novorossiya" highway (the M-14) to Crimea. The bands are roughly FPVs to 20 km, Hornet-type AI drones to 150 km, and FP-1/FP-2 to 200 km [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island].
  - The MoD launched the "Logistics Lockdown" programme on 27 May with an extra UAH 5 billion (about $112 million), paid through ePoints to the best-performing middle-strike units. The MoD claims a fourfold rise in destroyed Russian logistics at operational depth over the preceding months. It says Russian assaults along the line fall as logistics losses rise, and credits this jointly to middle strike and the Starlink loss [src:mod-2026-logistics-lockdown-launch]. The Kyiv Independent calls it "Logistical Lockdown".
  - Geolocated strikes rose from 55 (April) to 130+ (May). 125 trucks were hit and 80+ destroyed. Russia restricted traffic on the R-280 by decree on 21 May.
  - Brovdi said on 9 June that freight traffic on the M-14 from Rostov had fallen by 71%. From strike videos, OSINT analyst Clément Molin counted about ten Russian trucks hit per day by late May. The K-2 unit alone logged 258 strikes in April and 344 in May [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island].
  - By mid-June, Russian-installed officials said no intact bridges remained at Crimea's land entrances. Chonhar was unusable and pontoon replacements were struck [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island]. In July the MoD listed 14 rail and road bridges, overpasses and pontoon crossings hit in Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia oblasts and in Crimea, plus S-400, Buk and Pantsir systems and radars that protected the routes [src:mod-2026-middle-strike-july-results].
  - Gasoline rationing (20 litres) began in Crimea on 30 May, and Sevastopol sold out on 31 May. ISW judged middle strike the catalyst: long-range refinery strikes cut production, and middle strike stopped the remaining fuel reaching occupied Ukraine [src:isw-2026-06-04-gasoline-synergy].
  - Russia responded with camouflage, decoys, mobile fire teams and road netting. Fuel drivers were ordered into civilian clothes, and military fuel was moved in ambulances and bread vans [src:atlanticcouncil-2026-kirichenko-drones-logistics] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island].
  - The programme outlived its author. Zelenskyy dismissed Fedorov in July and appointed Drapatyi Commander-in-Chief. On 22 July acting minister Khmara, after meeting Drapatyi, said deep strike, middle strike and UGVs would be scaled up. Parliament confirmed Khmara as minister on 19 August [src:mod-2026-khmara-drapatyi-priorities] [src:euromaidanpress-2026-khmara-appointment].
- **Russian strikes on Ukrainian rail:** 209 locomotives, 86 rail bridges and 50 stations were damaged in 2025 and the first quarter of 2026. In frontline oblasts, buses are replacing trains on some routes [src:kyivindependent-2026-hodunova-ukrzaliznytsia].
- **Refineries:** Russian output fell about 13% in April–May 2026, with a possible 28% hit after mid-June strikes on the Moscow area. There were shortages in Crimea and the occupied territories [src:carnegie-2026-vakulenko-refineries].
## 10. Game/sim relevance

- **FPV on-screen display (OSD):**
  - The blocky white telemetry text over FPV strike clips comes from flight-controller OSDs such as Betaflight's. Elements sit on a **character grid**: 30×16 for PAL and 30×13 for NTSC on MAX7456 analogue chips, and a default 53×20 for HD digital systems. Fonts are uploaded as glyph sets [src:betaflight-osd-tab].
  - Standard elements include timers, alarms, warnings and a post-flight statistics screen [src:betaflight-osd-tab].
  - A game HUD built on a monospace glyph grid reads instantly as "drone feed."
- **Signal breakup:** analogue static and freeze at impact or under EW is the other signature of FPV footage. This is an observation, not sourced here.
- **Thermal:** night drone and sight footage is usually monochrome "white-hot" (hot = white) or "black-hot" (hot = black). The DJI Mavic 3T, a commercial thermal drone, records thermal video at 640×512 and 30 fps and offers White Hot, Black Hot, Tint, Iron Red, Hot Iron, Arctic, Medical, Fulgurite and two Rainbow palettes [src:dji-mavic3-enterprise-specs]. "Ironbow" is FLIR's name for the iron-red family. Which palette Ukrainian units prefer is not sourced; the monochrome modes dominate published strike clips (observation).
- **Geolocation proofs:** GeoConfirmed publishes a public "geolocation breakdown" for each event. This is the OSINT genre of annotated side-by-side frame and satellite comparisons with matched landmarks [src:geoconfirmed-home].
- **AI detections:** Avengers adds machine classifications of vehicles over live streams [src:wikipedia-delta]. In the game this could appear as auto-tagged boxes in a "Vezha" feed panel.
- **Map overlays:**
  - DeepState's attack arrows, and Black Bird's paired RU/UA front lines with movement arrows [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:blackbirdgroup-map].
  - ISW's dashed outline for infiltration (dashed = uncertain/anticipated, echoing APP-6) [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain] [src:wikipedia-nato-joint-military-symbology].

markdown:
- **Force generation.** Russia shifted from BTGs to divisions and regiments, fixing armies and divisions to axes while rotating battalions. Commanders stay on familiar ground; Ukraine struggled to match this until the corps reform [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
- **Recruitment is money-driven.** Prisoners of war describe their motives as mainly financial. Death payments are large enough to change a family's standard of living, while payments for wounds are being cut [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments]. Russia contracted more than 400,000 in 2024 [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments]. HUR counts 403,000 in 2025 against a 2026 plan of 409,000 [src:euromaidan-2025-murdoch-budanov-403k]. Budget-derived counts show Q1 2026 at a three-year low of 71,216 [src:kluge-2026-recruitment], even as regional bonuses hit record averages of about 1.5M RUB [src:united24-2026-litnarovych-bonuses]. By Ukrainian estimates, 2026 is the first year in which losses outrun recruitment, so a mobilization contingency of 300,000 a year is being prepared [src:euromaidan-2026-thomas-mobilization-600k] [src:euromaidan-2026-midttun-losses-recruits]. A senior Ukrainian official estimates that Russia needs about 400,000 recruits a year just to stand still [src:kyivindependent-2026-hyatt-nk-mobilization].
- **Who dies.** Among the Russian dead confirmed by name to September 2026, the largest groups are contract soldiers (88,600) and volunteers (80,679). Prisoners (26,979) and mobilized men (20,350) follow [src:kyivindependent-2026-hyatt-mediazona]. Volunteers are usually over 30 and mobilized men over 25, while early-war dead were 21–23-year-old regulars [src:mediazona-2026-casualties-count].
- **Penal and expendable troops.** Wagner convicts (2022–23), then Storm-Z (until August 2023), then Storm-V (no pardon, contract until the end of the war) [src:ukrpravda-2024-isw-storm-v]. Ukrainian troops report drugs, retreating soldiers being shot, and threats of being "zeroed" [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder] [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- **Engineering is a Russian strength.** Two engineer companies per brigade, doctrinal belts of defences, heavy mining, and concrete command posts [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Russian formations seed mixed AP and AT minefields systematically, while Ukraine, short of mines, seeds only the axes where it expects attacks [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments]. Rocket (Zemledeliye) and artillery remote mining close routes deep behind the line [src:euromaidan-2026-mukhina-zemledeliye]. Glide bombs (over 70,000 UMPK kits ordered for 2025) demolish Ukrainian positions, and "no fortification offers adequate protection" [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- **Adaptation is reactive.** Russia gets better at the problems in front of it but struggles to anticipate new ones [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Its answer to the kill zone was cheaper, faster and smaller units: motorcycles, then infiltration. Its dependence on Starlink became a single point of failure in February 2026 [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-air-assault-south].
- **Drone interdiction as an arm of its own.** Rubikon is a well-funded drone centre of about 5,000. It interdicts roads such as Izium–Sloviansk and hunts Ukrainian drone crews [src:euromaidan-2025-mukhina-rubikon-izium].
- **Allies.** North Korean infantry (2024–25) learned fast but at heavy cost [src:frontelligence-2025-nk-lessons]. Later deployments shifted to demining and construction (1,000 sappers and 5,000 builders announced in June 2025) [src:euromaidan-2025-zoria-nk-restoration]. By 2026 the troops were artillery and reconnaissance units on regular rotation [src:koreatimes-2026-yonhap-nk-kursk]. A further 10,000 are reportedly being prepared [src:kyivindependent-2026-hyatt-nk-mobilization].

# Bradley vs T-90M near Stepove (vignette)

Research base for *bavovniatko*. The player is the Ukrainian side. Accessed 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-30. Sources are listed in `sources/01-drones-uncrewed.yaml` and cited inline as `[src:<id>]`. Figures from officials and manufacturers are claims, and the text names who makes each one.

Oct 2022 – May 2025, peaking Feb – Mar 2024. The western and southern Black Sea off occupied Crimea (Sevastopol, Donuzlav, Alupka, Cape Tarkhankut, the Kerch Strait) and Novorossiysk, with operators in Kyiv and launch areas off Odesa Oblast.

- **Russian fire superiority.** Russia averaged about 20,000 rounds a day, peaking above 32,000. More than 1,100 tube guns, in groups of 80–90 per brigade-sized grouping, gave a 12:1 advantage in May–June. A Ukrainian company position with about 3 km of frontage could take 6,000 rounds a day. Ukraine rarely exceeded 6,000 rounds a day in total, being short of both barrels and shells [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. Meatgrinder gives 20,000–60,000 rounds a day and about 12M for 2022 as a whole [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].
- **MLRS.** Uragan and Smerch were used at maximum range (35–70 km) and even against point targets. Russia fielded up to 10 EW complexes per 20 km of front, which degraded Ukrainian precision fires [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **Russian kill chain.** With the unit's own UAV, fires landed 3–5 min after detection. Through a fire-control HQ it took 20–30 min, and about 48 h at operational level. Guns stood 100–150 m apart and rarely displaced unless fired upon [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **UAV spotters were used up fast.** About 90% of Ukrainian UAVs were lost, a quadcopter lasted about 3 flights and a fixed-wing about 6, and only about a third of missions succeeded. The Orlan-10 stood out on the Russian side [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons].
- **HIMARS.** From late June, GMLRS systematically hit depots that had been mapped from Russian dependence on rail. RUSI marks this as the end of the Russian Donbas offensive [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. After the July 2022 strikes on C2 and depots, Russia could no longer stockpile ammunition beside its guns [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder].

markdown: ## 5. Russia's side as reported
## 1. Overview

**Who is ahead changes by domain and by era.**
- **2023: Russia led the tactical EW fight.** It fielded about one major EW system per 10 km of front, and Ukraine lost about 10,000 UAVs a month [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Zaluzhnyi counted about 60 types of modern Russian EW, and some weeks more than 2,000 Ukrainian drones were disabled [src:euromaidan-2023-voichuk-economist-ew]. Russia also blunted US GPS-guided munitions: Excalibur's hit rate fell from 55% to 6% [src:kyivpost-2024-chiu-gps-weapons].
- **2024–25: fibre and CRPA shifted the edge back to Russia.** Russia fielded fibre-optic FPVs first, from August 2024 in Kursk, and moved to multi-element CRPA antennas (Kometa-M) to beat Ukrainian GNSS jamming [src:kyivindependent-2025-farrell-fiber-optic; src:defenseexpress-2025-kometa-m-16]. A Ukrainian EW company commander dates the "collapse" of conventional frontline jamming to the end of 2024 [src:euromaidan-2025-zoria-jamming-fails].
- **2025: Ukraine answered in several ways at once.**
  - Mass production: EW output rose 340-fold in 2024, from more than 140 makers [src:militarnyi-2025-pryhodko-ew-340x].
  - GNSS jamming and spoofing (Lima, the backbone of the national Pokrova system) [src:kyivpost-2026-lima; src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-pokrova-lima].
  - Interceptor drones: first against reconnaissance UAVs, then against Shaheds [src:kse-2025-drone-innovations].
  - Terminal autonomy (TFL-1) [src:kyivpost-2025-orlova-tfl1].
  - Nets over logistics roads [src:euromaidan-2025-murdoch-net-tunnels].
- **February 2026 was the biggest single swing.** The Starlink whitelist cut Russia off from the satellite link that had become the backbone of its drone and assault C2 [src:ukrinform-2026-liskovych-starlink-c2; src:atlanticcouncil-2026-spencer-starlink-crisis]. Biletsky put the drop in Russian drone effectiveness at 20–40% in the first two weeks [src:isw-2026-feb-26-assessment].
- **Mid-2026: Russia rebuilt its links on the ground and began to in space.** Mesh relay chains now control Gerans 150–175 km out [src:militarnyi-2026-khomenko-mesh-175km], and the Rassvet constellation gives two windows of more than an hour a day over Ukraine [src:euromaidan-2026-vivdych-rassvet-windows]. In the strike war, jet Gerans outran the cheap propeller interceptors [src:united24-2026-place-jet-gerans].
## 7. Terms
## 4. Forces

- **Defiance: 2nd Russo-Ukrainian War 2022-?** (GMT; D. B. Dockter & Mark Herman) covers the Kyiv and Chernihiv campaigns from 24 Feb to about 1 Apr 2022 in 3–4 day turns. It has five political tracks (Zelenskyy, NATO, Lukashenko, Putin, Russian MoD), supply, drones/air/missiles, VOVK partisans and a solitaire bot. The GMT page read "At the Printer" [src:gmt-2025-defiance]. The designer diary folds drones into detection and recon-strike, abstracts EW, ties Russian supply to railheads within about 50 miles, and lets troop quality outweigh force ratios. It calls the game "a first draft of history" [src:insidegmt-2023-dockter-herman-defiance].
- **Ukrainian Crisis** (Brian Train; a print-and-play in March 2014, boxed by Hollandspiele in 2017) is the precedent for designing while events unfold. Players spend finite chits across force, diplomacy, propaganda and prestige, and the conflict may never turn kinetic [src:hollandspiele-2017-train-ukrainian-crisis].
- **Glory to the Heroes** (Maj Ed Farren, British Army; free print-and-play) is a grand-strategic design derived from Philip Sabin, with 150 km hexes, monthly turns, attrition, climate, strategic bombing and propaganda [src:paxsims-2023-farren-glory-to-the-heroes]. It shares its name with Deaf Tone's shooter but is unrelated.
- **Other BGG listings** found by search include *2022: Ukraine* (the first year), *Putin's War 2022*, *Ukraine 2022: Tabletop Wargame* and *To Kyiv!*. Only their existence is confirmed [src:bgg-2022-ukraine].
- **Professional use of hobby games.** The Farren game circulates through PAXsims as a teaching tool [src:paxsims-2023-farren-glory-to-the-heroes]. A commercial armour sim (Steel Beasts PE) was repurposed for Ukrainian staff training, covered in §5.

**The outcome the player must reproduce:**
- The T-90M is **mission-killed by 25 mm fire** from two Bradleys and then **destroyed by an FPV**. The crew flees on foot [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts].
- The Ukrainian trench holds. No Bradley loss is reported in this engagement [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner].
- **Contested date.** The brief's "Oct–Nov 2023" is not supported by the sources:
  - Forbes reports the video circulating on Friday 12 Jan 2024 [src:forbes-2024-axe-bradleys-t90].
  - Newsweek relays the War Archive channel's claim that it happened "on Thursday", i.e. 11 Jan 2024 [src:newsweek-2024-cole-bradley-t90].
  - The gunner says he had returned from Bradley training in Germany in December, so the duel cannot predate that month [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-gunner].
- **Who finished the tank.** Forbes suggests the 25 mm fire killed its driver and commander [src:forbes-2024-axe-bradleys-t90]. A master gunner says only that "might have" happened, and the second video shows the crew fleeing [src:twz-2024-altman-bradley-t90m-experts].

Russia answered with helicopters, Su-30SM jets, gunboats, booms and FPVs that hunted the drones at sea. Ukraine in turn armed its drones with missiles:
- **31 Dec 2024:** R-73 "SeeDragon" missiles fired from a Magura V5 downed at least one Mi-8 off Cape Tarkhankut. HUR later claimed two.
- **2 May 2025:** AIM-9M Sidewinders fired from Magura V7s downed at least one Su-30SM west of Novorossiysk. HUR claims two [src:gur-2024-mi8][src:eurosd-2025-magura-mi8-kills][src:twz-2025-altman-su30-aim9].

- **GMLRS arrived and devastated Russian C2 and logistics** in July 2022. Dispersed Russian air defence could not intercept it at first [src:rusi-2023-watling-meatgrinder]. Russian jamming later forced a US software change to GMLRS, and it widened JDAM error from about 5 m to about 30 m [src:wikipedia-zhitel].
- **Ukraine was already hunting emitters.** A second Zhitel was destroyed in May 2022 [src:militarnyi-2022-kushnikov-zhitel-kharkiv].

markdown:
1. **Starlink over Crimea (Sep 2022).**
   - *Decision:* Musk refused coverage around Crimea [src:wikipedia-starlink-war], and the first mission failed [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
   - *Response:* both programmes moved to redundant links [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate][src:wikipedia-sea-baby]. Starlink terminals still appear on Maguras in later photos [src:aviationist-2024-durso-magura-mi8].
2. **The SBU–maker split (end 2022).**
   - *Decision:* after disputes over quality, specification and budget, the SBU built its own Sea Baby and the maker went to HUR [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
   - *Consequence:* two families of drones with different design briefs (static targets vs ships at sea), plus inter-agency rivalry. HUR describes operators refusing to share target coordinates; it says results were best when the agencies co-planned, as at Novorossiysk [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
3. **Ships at sea vs harbours (2023–24).** Budanov chose to intercept ships "on duty or being repositioned" rather than force the harbour defences at Sevastopol and Novorossiysk [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate]. All three 2024 sinkings were of ships outside the main harbours [src:euromaidan-2024-zoria-six-maguras][src:pravda-2024-yusov-kunikov-crew][src:isw-2024-03-05-roca].
4. **Russia moves the fleet (Sep–Oct 2023).** The move followed the missile and USV strikes, including the 22 Sep strike on the BSF HQ. Satellite imagery shows the shift to Novorossiysk [src:wikipedia-storm-shadow][src:pravda-2023-mt-anderson-bsf-novorossiysk]. ISW credits the 2023 campaign with "sequestering" the BSF in the east [src:isw-2024-02-14-roca]. The alternative base at Ochamchire was too small (Ryzhenko) [src:hromadske-2024-ryzhenko-bsf].
5. **Ukraine opens its own corridor (Aug 2023).** Russia had declared merchant ships hostile. Kyiv registered ships and sent the *Joseph Schulte* on 16 Aug [src:maritimeexec-2023-joseph-schulte][src:pravda-2023-first-ship-corridor]. Volumes grew through 2024 [src:pravda-2024-corridor-45mt][src:osw-2024-record-exports].
6. **Retarget mid-mission (14 Feb 2024).** HUR's rule: don't interfere with the operators, and decide quickly when the plan breaks. The swarm switched to the *Kunikov* [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate].
7. **Russia changes commanders (Feb – Mar 2024).** Sokolov went after the *Kunikov* and Yevmenov after the *Kotov*. Shoigu ordered drills and extra guns [src:pravda-2024-ukdi-sokolov][src:hromadske-2024-ryzhenko-bsf][src:maritimeexec-2024-bsf-new-measures]. Milbloggers debated the "bureaucratic inertia" behind the losses [src:isw-2024-03-05-roca].
8. **Air cover against USVs leads to missiles on USVs (2024).**
   - *Russia* shifted to helicopters and Su-30SMs hunting drones offshore [src:isw-2024-12-31-roca].
   - *Ukraine:* Budanov had already named air defence on the drones as "the next step" in Mar 2024 [src:pravda-2024-romaniuk-magura-target-eliminate]. R-73s were seen in May 2024 [src:aviationist-2024-durso-magura-mi8], and the first kill came on 31 Dec 2024 [src:gur-2024-mi8].
9. **R-73 or AIM-9 (Jan 2025).** HUR began fitting AIM-9s and says "the best results [come from] the AIM-9" [src:twz-2025-altman-su30-aim9]. Group 13 still plans R-73 fits as an alternative [src:euromaidan-2025-zoria-magura-v7].
10. **Russia's response to the jet loss (May 2025).** Milbloggers argued for FPVs and ZALA–Lancet pairs instead of jets "firing cannons at USVs like in World War II". ISW records the call for coastal FPV integration [src:twz-2025-altman-su30-aim9][src:isw-2025-05-03-roca]. Russia's own Katran USV is reported as a threat to Maguras [src:defenseexpress-2025-magura-v7].

**Defining features.** Minefields, drones and Lancets, and precision fires made breaching columns predictable and targetable. Poor operational security meant Russia knew the axis and the timing. RUSI concluded that renewed Ukrainian offensives would not be viable "in the foreseeable future" [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
**The outcome the player must reproduce, by act:**

**Sub-phases.** The best split is at about Jun/Jul 2026, rather than at Vivaldi, which began in late spring.
- **e9a, late Jan–May 2026: the southern counterattacks.** Russia loses Starlink, Ukraine retakes 400+ km² on the Oleksandrivka axis by March, Russian net gains drop to near zero, and there are two holiday truces.
- **e9b, Jun–Sep 2026: strike war and a new command.** The jet-Geran surge, the Patriot shortage caused by the Iran war, the replacement of the defence minister and the commander-in-chief (16–21 Jul), the 745 km² claim for the Oleksandrivka offensive (Aug), Operation Vivaldi made public (Sep), and envoy diplomacy.

## 3. The diorama: geography, terrain, weather

**Dimensions.**
- Width and rows. Front-line belts are "typically three to four rows of trees deep" and "rarely more than twenty to thirty meters wide", with **10–30 m gaps** left for farm machinery [src:saratoga-2026-parfonov-treelines]. Belts mapped as narrow wood strips in OSM have a median canopy width of **20–27 m** in the sample boxes (§2.7) [src:osm-overpass-2026-landscape-sample]. Canopy width overstates the planted width: Ukrainian foresters convert remote-sensed canopy width to stem-to-stem width with a factor of 0.46 [src:matsala-2024-war-protective-plantations]. A studied Left-Bank forest-steppe oak windbreak is **15 m** wide, planted as oak "nests" at 5 × 3 m with 5 m alleys and companion and shrub rows [src:maliuha-2023-windbreaks]. A Luhansk soil-erosion study found about **10 m** to be the optimal width for trapping blown soil [src:tarasov-usda-luhansk-wind-erosion].
- Height. Mature belts reach **19.6–23.4 m** [src:maliuha-2023-windbreaks].
- Spacing. Parfonov describes a dense grid at "intervals of 300 to 400 meters longitudinally and 1,000 to 2,000 meters laterally" [src:saratoga-2026-parfonov-treelines]. The measurements put the main belts somewhat further apart. At Huliaipole the median is **549 m** (p10–p90 379–990 m) between main belts and about **1.1–1.3 km** between cross-belts. At Robotyne it is about 0.5–0.6 km and 1.0–1.2 km (§2.7) [src:osm-overpass-2026-landscape-sample] [src:eox-2021-s2cloudless]. In the Oleshky district of Kherson oblast the distance between belts is 350–780 m, averaging 550 m (search-only) [src:ffm-oleshky-shelterbelts]. With belts about 20 m tall, main belts therefore stand roughly 25–30 tree heights apart. This is a derived figure: Soviet design norms stated as multiples of height were not found.
- Density. Kherson oblast alone had about 30,000 km of windbreaks, roughly 1 km per km² of oblast [src:sudnik-2006-windbreaks-southern-ukraine]. A full two-way grid at the measured spacings implies about 2.5–3 km of belt per km² of cropland. The best-mapped OSM boxes reach 1.35 km/km² (§2.7).
- Orientation. In Luhansk oblast the main harmful (deflation) winds come from the east [src:tarasov-usda-luhansk-wind-erosion]. Main belts are laid across the prevailing wind, so they tend to run roughly north–south there. The measured grids are near-cardinal at Huliaipole (N–S main belts, E–W cross-belts) and Robotyne (roughly E–W and N–S, 10° off). They are oblique (WNW–ESE and NNE–SSW) east of Kupiansk and irregular in the dissected ground south of Chasiv Yar (§2.7).
- Species. Oak, pine, birch and poplar form the tall layer, with linden, maple, apple and pear lower down [src:eou-shelterbelt]. Oak-led belts with companion trees and a shrub understorey are common [src:maliuha-2023-windbreaks].

- **Three acts, three verbs.** Act 1 is a *logistics-and-deception board*, like Spiderweb's long game: route, paperwork, scanner-defeating packaging and an unwitting driver. It ends in one timing decision on the bridge. Act 2 is a *night USV run*: thermal view, two boats, two directions. Act 3 is *covert placement over months*, then a single command.
- **"Running the barricades" must track the real build-up.** No floating or sunken barrier is reported before Aug 2023, and Russian critics blamed neglected maritime security for Act 2 [src:isw-2023-07-17-roca; ukranews-2022-how-bridge-guarded]. The full layered system (§5 table) only existed from 2024. Act 2 should not face 2024 defences. The barrier layer is best played as the *what-if pressure between acts*: the Aug–Sep 2023 attempts and the Aug 2024 claims. In Act 3 the barrier sits on the surface and the charges go beneath it.
- **Storms are an ally.** Barrier integrity degrades with weather. Real storms flooded, scattered or set adrift all seven boom barges in Nov 2023 and most of 36 in late 2024 [src:espreso-2023-storm-barrier; unn-2025-bridge-protection-restored]. Russia rebuilds over weeks.
- **Win bands:**
  - Act 1: 2–3 road spans down plus a fuel-train fire, and the bridge partly open the same day [src:wikipedia-2022-crimean-bridge-explosion; isw-2022-10-08-roca].
  - Act 2: 1 span down and 1 displaced, rail open within hours, full repair in about three months [src:isw-2023-07-17-roca; meduza-2023-bridge-repaired].
  - Act 3: an explosion at the supports and a closure of hours. The damage band runs from "no damage" (Kremlin) to "emergency condition" with a ≤5 t limit afterwards (SBU) [src:kyivindependent-2025-fornusek-kremlin-no-damage; pravda-2025-prots-third-strike; ssu-2025-maliuk-hallmark].
  - Over-performing, by destroying the bridge, should not count as the historical win.
- **Consequence scripting.** After Act 1, a scripted Russian missile wave hits Ukrainian cities [src:isw-2022-10-10-roca]. After Act 2, the Odesa strikes and the end of the grain deal [src:pravda-2023-peskov-odesa-revenge; isw-2023-07-17-roca]. After every act, Russian logistics shift: ferry queues, the land corridor, weight limits.
- **The real payoff is logistics, not rubble.** Show the diversion: trucks to ferries (2022), military rail falling to 4–5 trains a day (2024), then ferries destroyed and a ≤5 t bridge (2025–26) [src:molfar-2024-bridge-satellite; ssu-2025-maliuk-hallmark; rusi-2026-ferris-logistics-targeting]. The coda can be a logistics overlay that ties into the 2026 "island Crimea" campaign [src:euromaidanpress-2026-crimea-island].
- **Pacing.** Act 1's prep runs for months, compressed, and its strike lasts seconds. Act 2 is two impacts minutes apart: about 5 minutes on the SBU's CCTV, 16 minutes between the explosions reported by Russian channels (03:04 and 03:20) [src:cnn-2023-walsh-sea-baby; twz-2023-altman-kerch-closed]. Act 3's placement is undisclosed: the dossier has no detail, so do not invent a mini-game the sources cannot support.

**Key battles and operations.** Mariupol falls (May). Russia's Donbas offensive takes **Sievierodonetsk** (June) and then Lysychansk [src:wikipedia-russo-ukrainian-war]. Ukraine's Kherson operation begins on **29 Aug 2022**, which is the hinge into e3 [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**Key battles and operations.** A multi-axis invasion from Belarus, Russia and Crimea hits Kyiv (Hostomel, Bucha, Irpin), Chernihiv, Sumy, Kharkiv, and the south (Kherson taken, Mariupol besieged). Russia planned a roughly 10-day operation and expected occupation by August 2022. Its deception worked, but it had no contingency plan when speed failed [src:rusi-2022-zabrodskyi-preliminary-lessons]. By early April Russia had abandoned the attempt on Kyiv and the north [src:wikipedia-russo-ukrainian-war]. The Mariupol siege ran on into May (e2).
section: 3. Per-era notes / e1-invasion (24 Feb – early Apr 2022)

markdown:
**Main units.**
- **The 155th Guards Naval Infantry Brigade.** Pacific Fleet, from Vladivostok and Primorsky Krai [src:dfrlab-2023-vuhledar-war-report].
  - It had been rebuilt after Kyiv and after Pavlivka. A captured marine said it was 80–90% mobilised men [src:isw-2023-02-13-roca].
  - Its strength is contested. Ukraine claimed about 5,000 [src:politico-2023-melkozerova-155th-brigade]. Kyiv Post put it at about 2,000 at full strength [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-vuhledar-marines]. Forbes said the 155th and 40th together had about 6,000 at their peak [src:forbes-2022-axe-marines-pavlivka].
- **The 40th Naval Infantry Brigade.** Pacific Fleet, from Kamchatka, an Arctic-trained unit [src:forbes-2022-axe-marines-pavlivka] [src:rferl-2023-eckel-what-happened-vuhledar]. Each marine brigade has motorised battalions, a tank battalion, engineers, artillery and air defence [src:forbes-2022-axe-marines-pavlivka].
- **Eastern Military District army units.**
  - The 29th Combined Arms Army's 36th Motor Rifle Brigade [src:isw-2023-01-31-roca] [src:isw-2023-02-09-roca].
  - The 36th Combined Arms Army's 37th Motor Rifle and 5th Guards Tank Brigades [src:isw-2023-03-01-roca].
- **The 3rd Army Corps.** This was a volunteer corps formed in 2022. It included the 72nd Motor Rifle Brigade with the Tatar "Alga" battalion (about 500 men at the highest estimate) and the Chuvash "Atal" battalion [src:isw-2023-02-09-roca] [src:dfrlab-2023-vuhledar-war-report].
- **Others named by a Ukrainian reserve officer:**
  - the 136th Motor Rifle Brigade (Southern Military District, which arrived in March [src:isw-2023-03-10-roca])
  - the DNR's "Kaskad" and "Vostok" units
  - BARS (Combat Reserve) volunteers
  - the "Patriot" private military company [src:isw-2023-02-10-roca]
- **Also reported:** the 14th Spetsnaz Brigade and Akhmat-North elements [src:dfrlab-2023-vuhledar-war-report], the 5th Brigade of the 1st Corps in March [src:novayagazeta-2023-5th-brigade-appeal], and T-80/T-90s of the "90th Tank Regiment" [src:kyivpost-2023-korshak-vuhledar-marines].

- **ISW's methodology page** still returns 403, and the Wayback copy of the 26 Sep 2026 ROCA does not repeat the "furthest assessed extent" sentence. That wording rests on pass-1 search excerpts. ISW's historic 2022 legend (e.g., "Ukrainian counteroffensives" on static maps) was not checked visually.
- **November 2025 and 2024-total mismatches.** DeepState was quoted at "some 630" km² for November 2025 and 3,600+ km² for 2024, against 503 and 3,301 computed. May 2026 also has conflicting DeepState quotations (14 net per RFE/RL; 130 lost and 250 regained per Kyiv Post). DeepState's own Telegram monthly posts, which would settle these, were not fetched.
- **Event-dated series.** The computed series follows publication dates. Reassigning OPSEC-delayed Ukrainian gains (e.g., Vivaldi, May–June 2026) to their event months would need DeepState's changelog text parsed per settlement.
- **Suriyak's legend and cadence** are known only from editors' descriptions. Its maps are images on X and Telegram (X was not fetchable). Andrew Perpetua's map data file did not load outside the web app, so its polygon legend (as opposed to its event badges) is unverified.
- **Liveuamap's legend** is not documented by the site. The side-colour reading comes from 19 captured events, and the live site blocks fetches.
- **UA Control Map** legend and terms are unverified (the site returned only a 226-byte redirect stub).
- **NYT "Maps: Tracking the Russian Invasion"** is blocked directly and through the Wayback Machine. Its methodology is unknown. The Kyiv Independent map pages were not fetched.
- **DeepState's official terms of use** were not found. It is unclear whether the `/api/history/*` endpoints are tolerated for third-party use, so ask before any bulk use.
- **Delta's visual design** (basemap, symbol set, colours) is not described in any fetched source. The NATO ACT "DELTA at CWIX24" article is still behind a Cloudflare challenge.
- **Thermal and FPV visuals.** No source was found on which palette Ukrainian units prefer, or on analogue "signal loss" artefacts under EW. FLIR's palette guides are behind Cloudflare.
- **GeoConfirmed commercial use** is not addressed by its API terms. Written permission is needed before shipping any of its data.
- **Date conflict:** the Makarivka encirclement dispute is dated December 2024 by dev.ua. A Wikipedia summary placed it in December 2023. dev.ua's date is used.
## 7. Terms

**Command.**
- The Eastern Military District and Eastern Grouping of Forces were under Col. Gen. Rustam Muradov, appointed 5 Oct 2022 [src:moscowtimes-2023-muradov-dismissed] [src:isw-2023-02-10-roca].
- The 155th Brigade was commanded by Col. Zurab Akhmedov in Nov 2022 [src:isw-2022-11-07-roca].
- Unofficial Russian sources reported a special forces colonel, Sergey Polyakov, killed while commanding in the assault [src:cnn-2023-lister-vuhledar-turkeys].
Russian Telegram footage, such as the Iskander strike, the 2 July mine drops and the flag-raising, is known only through the sources above. It is not linked here.
## 5. Systems and tactics in use

**Weather and light.** These are Open-Meteo ERA5 reanalysis values queried 2026-10-01 [src:open-meteo-historical-weather], not observations. The moon is computed from the mean synodic month and is approximate.
- **14 Jan 2024, Kyrylivka, 21:00:** full overcast (100%), about 2 °C, southerly wind of about 31 km/h, light precipitation. Sunset was at 17:16, so it was full night, and the moon was a thin crescent (about 3 days old). This was a night radar fight with no visual element until the fireball the Su-30 pilot saw [src:twz-2024-altman-rogoway-a50-claims].
- **23 Feb 2024, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, 18:00–19:00:** mostly clear (28% → 1% cloud), about 5–6 °C, easterly wind of about 14–17 km/h. Sunset was at 18:03 Kyiv time, and the moon was near full. If HUR's 18:45 is Kyiv time (the source does not say), the kill came in dusk, which fits the crash videos [src:twz-2024-newdick-second-a50].
- **26 Feb 2023, Machulishchy, morning:** overcast, about −3 °C, north-westerly wind of about 20 km/h. Snow on the airframe is one reason the imagery was inconclusive [src:ukrinform-2023-machulishchy-satellite].

**Strikes on Ukrainian logistics.**
- Geran/Shahed and Gerbera drones fly in waves against airfields, training areas, transformer substations and industry [src:rusi-2025-watling-tactical-developments].
- The rail campaign targets locomotives and bridges [src:kyivindependent-2026-hodunova-ukrzaliznytsia].
- Rubikon-style FPV interdiction of roads reaches 15–30 km [src:euromaidanpress-2026-mukhina-net-tunnels-1000km].

- **Interdiction as the main lever.** Give each crossing a capacity state (open, light vehicles only, closed, destroyed) and a repair rate. HIMARS salvoes of about 8 rockets degrade a bridge for days or weeks, and repairs invite re-strikes [src:isw-2022-07-20-roca] [src:isw-2022-07-27-roca] [src:isw-2022-08-25-roca]. Model ferries and barges as low-capacity, mobile, regenerating crossings that must be re-found each time. They are worth striking mainly when the ground offensive is active [src:isw-2022-08-30-roca].
- **Scarce launchers.** About 16 US launchers plus M270/MARS were shared across the whole front [src:defenseone-2022-tucker-milley-himars] [src:pravda-2022-reznikov-four-himars]. Every salvo sent to Kherson is one not sent to Kharkiv. No source quantifies the GMLRS stock, so treat it as a tunable parameter.
- **The Russian supply meter.** Throughput should fall but never reach zero. Kherson "did not starve", and Russia fought until withdrawal [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal]. The historical script: bridges closed by mid-August, the right bank untenable by late October.
- **Ground pacing.** Expect a slow and costly August–September (about 1,440 km² of net gain by 7 November in our window), a sudden northern collapse on 1–4 October, and a 3-day Russian collapse to the river on 9–11 November (about 4,570 km²) [src:deepstate-api-history] [src:isw-2022-10-04-roca]. Losses should be steep against prepared lines, with drones and counter-battery working against the attacker [src:stripes-2022-hudson-kherson-toll].
- **The pinning effect.** Pressure at Kherson drew Russian reserves south and so opened Kharkiv [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. The debrief can link to chapter 6.
- **Win band.** Ukraine reaches the Dnipro along the whole right bank by about 11–12 November, Kherson city is entered on 11 November, and Russia withdraws 20,000–42,000 men and most of its heavy equipment. Bonus scoring for Russian equipment caught in the crossing should stay modest, because the historical haul was small [src:isw-2022-11-11-roca] [src:wavellroom-2023-miller-kherson-withdrawal]. The bridges always end up dropped by Russia.
- **Water as a hazard.** Inhulets flooding (14 Sep) and the drawdown of the Kakhovka reservoir are scripted events, and striking the dam should exist as a forbidden "last resort" option [src:pravda-2022-kryvyi-rih-dam] [src:wikipedia-2022-kherson-counteroffensive].

**What Ukraine had.**
- **Western armour** was pledged in Jan 2023 [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - Leopard 2A4s arrived in February–March 2023 and German 2A6s in March, with Challenger 2s from March [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine] [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].
  - Bradleys arrived from April 2023. The US total passed 300 [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine] [src:state-2025-us-security-cooperation-ukraine].
- **Patriot.** Crews were trained in early 2023 [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons]. The first US and German batteries arrived in April [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine], and the Air Force put a second battery on combat duty on 27 Apr 2023 [src:ukrinform-2023-second-patriot].
- **Storm Shadow** arrived before May 2023 [src:oryx-heavy-weaponry-supplied-ukraine].
- **Bakhmut costs.** Around Bakhmut about 10,000 Ukrainian troops were killed or severely wounded. From February, Russia had artillery control of the city's supply roads [src:rusi-2024-watling-offensive-lessons].

**2026 turn (e9).** In February 2026 Russia lost Starlink, which "blinded headquarters" [src:euromaidan-2026-zoria-air-assault-south]. Ukraine began local counteroffensives: the Air Assault Forces in eastern Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia, and the 3rd Army Corps' **Operation Vivaldi** near Lyman. Vivaldi's key idea was to kill the *reinforcement and supply* of Russian infiltration groups rather than chase every infiltrator [src:mwi-2026-rose-vivaldi] [src:isw-2026-09-26-assessment] [src:kyivindependent-2026-farrell-vivaldi].

The whole group is 300–500 m deep. Supporting guns sit 8–12 km back and mortars 2–3 km back, and belt intersections are avoided as command-post sites because they are obvious aiming points [src:saratoga-2026-parfonov-treelines]. In spring 2026 Russian forces tried to use new foliage to move infantry along treelines on foot, on motorcycles or on quad bikes [src:rferl-2026-lohinov-spring-battlefield].
- Survival. Near Pokrovsk in winter 2024–25, an exposed 80 × 30 m trench cut into the 1 km-long CHAI treeline was destroyed. Two concealed fighting holes in the undergrowth held for 10 days [src:wotr-2026-maurin-front-line].
- Foliage. Leaves protected positions from drones and precision fires in summer 2023. Autumn leaf-fall and then snow exposed them [src:cepa-2023-kallberg-treelines]. Parfonov writes that summer canopy "substantially degrade[s]" FPV effectiveness. Foliage conceals both sides from late spring to early autumn, and bare branches expose both from late autumn to early spring [src:saratoga-2026-parfonov-treelines].
- Being shredded. Sustained barrages reduced some treelines to "piles of split wood and tree branches" [src:cepa-2023-kallberg-treelines]. Shredded belts become "tangles of fallen timber" that are impassable and useless to both sides, effectively grey zones [src:saratoga-2026-parfonov-treelines].

- **DeepState:**
  - No documented public API or open licence was found. The web app itself calls JSON endpoints [src:deepstate-api-history]:
    - `…/api/history/public`: a list of every map version with UA/EN changelog text and timestamps.
    - `…/api/history/{id}/geojson`: the full map of any listed version (the basis of §2.7).
    - `…/api/history/last`: a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with KML-style `fill`/`stroke`/`styleUrl` properties and trilingual names (`Ukrainian /// English /// i18n key`).
  - Community scrapers:
    - **cyterat/deepstate-map-data** (GPL-3.0 code): daily GeoJSON since 2024-07-08, merging "Occupied", "CADR and CALR" and "Occupied Crimea" into one occupied multipolygon, plus a consolidated gzip history [src:github-cyterat-deepstate-map-data].
    - Others found on GitHub include a KML exporter and a GIF generator (not individually cited).
  - The scraper's GPL covers the *code*, not DeepState's data. DeepState has objected to unauthorised commercial overlays (Polymarket) [src:wikipedia-deepstatemap-live].
  - **For a commercial game, ask DeepState for permission** or use it only as an internal reference.
- **ISW/CTP:**
  - The layers are public ArcGIS Feature Services, queryable via REST, e.g. `VIEW_RussiaCoTinUkraine_V2`, `View_AssessedRussianInfiltrationAreasinUkraine_V4`, `VIEW_ClaimedUkrainianCounteroffensives_V2`, `RUAF_Field_Fortifications_Polylines`.
  - Every item states: "This geodata is the exclusive intellectual property of the Institute for the Study of War (ISW). You may not use this geodata without the written consent of ISW." [src:isw-arcgis-control-of-terrain]
- **ACLED:**
  - Non-commercial use is covered by a royalty-free, non-exclusive licence. Commercial businesses need a corporate licence and governments a public-sector licence.
  - No direct access to raw data may be given. Derivatives must be "transformative," and attribution is mandatory [src:acled-eula].
  - The monitor needs a login for curated files [src:acled-ukraine-conflict-monitor].
- **GeoConfirmed:**
  - The API spec states that read endpoints need no authentication and that the data is "freely available for research, journalism, and analytical use". It offers per-conflict KMZ, CSV and GeoJSON exports.
  - There is no licence field and no mention of commercial use. It asks for a descriptive User-Agent and fair use, and to "get in touch" for bulk or near-real-time needs [src:geoconfirmed-openapi].
  - For a commercial game, ask. Its icon *grammar* (type × state × actor colour) is an idea and can be reimplemented freely.
- **Liveuamap:** the terms (Jan 2023 snapshot) allow use of "our data and maps, including map tiles and areas polygons partially, or in the whole in your work, with reference to liveuamap.com". Third-party images and text stay under their platforms' terms [src:liveuamap-about-terms]. The API is paid: Pro at $150/month for 200 requests/day, Enterprise from $1,000/month [src:liveuamap-promo-api].
- **One-person maps:** AMK Mapping's Google My Map exports as KML [src:amk-mapping-control-map], and Andrew Perpetua's map asks for screenshots rather than embeds [src:perpetua-ukrdailyupdate-map]. Neither states a licence, so treat both as reference only. Suriyak publishes images [src:suriyak-telegram].
- **Black Bird Group:** presented as a public product and welcomed in non-profit or public-facing adaptations. There is no formal licence, so ask [src:blackbirdgroup-map].
- **Symbology:** milsymbol is MIT and fine to ship [src:github-milsymbol]. Battle Staff Tools is proprietary [src:spatialillusions-battle-staff-tools].
- **Recommendation:** ship the game with **self-authored, simplified historical control polygons** (e.g. digitised by hand at era granularity, informed by these maps). Credit DeepState, ISW and Black Bird as inspiration, and request explicit permission before bundling any of their geometry.

Replacing them needs the ISW archive for 2022–2024 via Wayback (slow and rate-limited) or searches that the budget did not allow.
